request.hypothesis: Material editing may affect shared material data: local_material mutates the existing material without copying it, and the block and all chair meshes share SceneActSurface_0. A seat color edit could therefore propagate to parts intended to remain green.
request.observation: The separate block on the right is green in reference image 1 but blue in reconstruction image 2. The chair back and legs show the same color discrepancy, while the seat is blue in both.

alternatives.explanation: The block could have received an incorrect blue color directly, independently of shared-material propagation.
alternatives.predicted_probe_phenomenon: Isolating Box.008 leaves its surfaces blue because its material assignment and base color remain unchanged.

alternatives.explanation: Scene-dependent illumination or reflected blue light could contribute to the apparent color, although the explicit blue base color makes this less likely as the principal cause.
alternatives.predicted_probe_phenomenon: Removing other meshes could reduce a reflected color cast; movement toward green would support a scene-interaction contribution.

request.probe_reason: Isolate hides other meshes while retaining the visible block, testing whether its blue appearance depends on surrounding geometry. Persistent blue supports an intrinsic material explanation but cannot distinguish shared-data mutation from a directly incorrect assignment.

execution.interpretation: Controlled observation, not proof of causal attribution or true 3D accuracy

probes.interpretation: Controlled sensitivity, not unique causal attribution
